Issue 1

🚢 Rising Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz - Tanker Attacks, Drone Seizures, US Carrier Reinforcements

Key summary
  • Al Jazeera reported that tankers in the Strait of Hormuz were hit by mine attacks and a drone alert was issued near an Iraqi gas field, with Iran claiming the tankers were struck by mines. The IRGC announced that in the early hours of November 17, it seized a US MQM-170 drone near Qeshm Island using electronic warfare (the 9th drone seized).
  • A third US Navy aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, and tensions continued to rise amid Iran's ongoing blockade. Iranian Army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia stated that reopening the Strait of Hormuz would only be possible if the conditions set by Iran are accepted, raising concerns over a prolonged blockade.
  • According to Reuters, despite tensions in the Gulf region, international oil prices fell amid forecasts of oversupply.

Issue 3

🕊️ Gulf and Regional Tension-Easing Diplomacy - Chinese Envoy Tour, Saudi-Qatar Coordination

Key summary
  • China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that Middle East envoy Zhai Jun toured three countries—Iran, Oman, and Saudi Arabia—in mediation efforts to ease tensions in the Gulf region and seek a political resolution to the Yemen issue.
  • Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan discussed ways to ease regional tensions in a phone call on Monday, November 16, and the Qatari Prime Minister also held a separate call with the Saudi Foreign Minister.
  • In the Yemeni civil war, Houthi rebels advanced on the interim capital Aden, and Saudi Arabia abruptly replaced the commander of the anti-Houthi coalition forces. The Arab Interior Ministers' Council condemned the Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia.

🇧🇭 Bahrain - IRGC Attacks Linked to Iran and Controversy over Shia Suppression

Key summary
  • US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the IRGC's attack on Bahrain in a phone call with Bahraini Interior Minister Al Zayani. Bahrain is reported to have faced retaliatory attacks from Iran since the US-Iran war.
  • Bahrain's High Criminal Court sentenced 64 people, including Shia clerics, to life imprisonment for involvement in a terrorist organization linked to Iran's IRGC, raising controversy over religious suppression under Sunni royal rule.

This page automatically collects and summarizes public news coverage and material from relevant institutions across Qatar, Iran, other major countries and Korea. News is gathered by querying Google News RSS feeds, Naver News search, and outlet RSS (Al Jazeera, BBC, etc.) with keywords such as Qatar, the Middle East and energy; in-depth reports are collected directly from the publication boards and RSS of domestic and international research institutes, international organizations and consultancies (supplemented by news search targeting those publishers), keeping only analyses and reports on the Middle East situation, the Iran war and their industrial, supply-chain and energy repercussions. The report list accumulates items published since the war's outbreak (2026-02-28), split into domestic and overseas and ordered by publication date (newest first). Collection and summarization rely on each outlet's publicly available headline and snippet; for subscription or paywalled outlets, the full article can be opened through the provided source link only after the reader signs in or subscribes to that outlet directly. The collected articles are automatically clustered and summarized by issue, and translated into English and Arabic, by Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5) AI. The whole process runs and publishes automatically twice a day (07:00 and 15:30 Qatar time) via GitHub Actions. The Qatar government activity section separately curates only official statements, announcements and actions on the war and regional situation by Qatar government and state entities — the Emir, the Prime Minister, the ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defense and Interior, the Government Communications Office (GCO), QatarEnergy and the state news agency (QNA). Owing to automated collection some articles or reports may be missed, so please re-verify important issues against the original sources and further searches.
